reason: Both plans satisfy all hard requirements, but Response B's metrics/halt-condition section is more rigorous, giving four distinct numeric thresholds (payment failure rate, discrepancy rate, API error rate, P95 latency) each tied to a specific rolling time window, whereas Response A supplies only one true numeric halt threshold and labels its other triggers as explicitly non-numeric. B's batch math is also internally consistent (5×2,000=10,000 for Phase 2), while A's Phase 3 sub-wave math (5×15%=75%) doesn't quite match the stated 73%.
